tagline.text: A Holy Week pilgrimage site with giant Stations of the Cross sculptures along a hillside

location.label: Location
location.text: Hill behind St. James Church, Iguig, Cagayan

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: December–May dry season; Holy Week is crowded

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱200–1,500 (per person, round-trip transport from Tuguegarao and snacks)

children.text: Iguig Calvary Hills is a pilgrimage site where the 14 Stations of the Cross are laid out as large sculptures on the hill behind a red-brick church on the Cagayan River. Close to Tuguegarao, it is widely visited for Holy Week pilgrimages and church tours.

Iguig Calvary Hills is a wide hillside park behind the parish church of St. James the Apostle (Santiago) in Iguig, Cagayan. The 14 Stations of the Cross are set up around the hill as sculptures much taller than a person, and the site is said to have been created in 1982 from an idea of the then parish priest, Fr. Rogelio Cortez. The area is about 11 hectares, and the part where the sculptures stand is described as roughly 4 hectares. The sculptures are said to be close to 6 meters tall, so they stand out even from a distance.
Iguig is an old town that began as a Spanish mission in 1608, on the lower Cagayan River not far from Tuguegarao. According to Wikipedia it is about
14km
from Tuguegarao and about
495km

from Manila overland. St. James Church is a red-brick building completed in 1787, notable for its arched buttresses supporting the rear walls, and it was declared a National Historical Landmark in 1939. These buttresses are presented as an example of earthquake Baroque, and some say the facade has been altered and no longer looks as it once did. The name Iguig is said to come from the land of Ig, an old chieftain and warrior, and today the town is made up of 23 barangays. Because the Cagayan River flows beside the town, people and goods long moved along it, and the brick stairway leading down from the church to the river suggests the path used in those days.

Calvary Hills is a hill for praying as you walk. You follow the stations in order from the first to the fourteenth, meditating on the Passion of Christ, so even if you are not a believer the scale of the sculptures and the views from the hill leave an impression. During Holy Week pilgrims come from all over the country and prayers of the Way of the Cross continue, while at other times it is quiet and pleasant for walking. Behind the church a brick stairway leads down toward the Cagayan River and an old well remains, so it also works as a historical walk. Each sculpture is expressed with large faces and postures, so even from far away you can read the scene from the silhouette alone. Between the paths there is grass and shade from trees, which makes for slow walking, and there are places to sit here and there, so families on pilgrimage can go round comfortably.

This guide is for travelers planning a day trip with Tuguegarao as their base. Since traveling just for one site can be long, we recommend a church tour that combines it with Piat Basilica or Tuguegarao Cathedral. During Holy Week events and traffic controls make it very different from usual, so check the parish and the municipal office announcements for the schedule and entry arrangements. Accounts of the entrance fee differ, with some saying it is free and others about ₱20, so it is safest to confirm locally. Transport options and times vary by report, but in general it takes a little over 30 minutes from Tuguegarao to Iguig. Look up Iguig Calvary Hills in a map app to check the route, and on site ask for directions using St. James Church as your reference and people will readily point the way. If you come from Manila by long-distance bus, get off in Tuguegarao and transfer; if you see an old church along the way, stopping briefly can help you get a feel before your visit.

Large concrete sculptures shaping each scene stand around the hill. The sculptures are described as about 6 meters tall, and the route follows the station numbers, so there is little worry about getting lost. The 14 Stations show the scenes in order from the condemnation to the burial in the tomb, so if you pause at each sculpture and reflect on the meaning of the scene, your walk becomes deeper.

A red-brick church completed in 1787, standing side by side with Calvary Hills. The arched buttresses at the back are distinctive, and many people photograph them for architecture. Some say the facade has been altered and looks different from before. The church is a parish of the Archdiocese of Tuguegarao, and Masses are held at set times. Check the parish announcements for exact times.
Behind the church are arched buttresses supporting the walls and a brick stairway leading down toward the river. It is a good place to rest while looking at the Cagayan River.

From the hill you can look down over the Cagayan River and the surrounding plain. The view is best around sunset on a clear day. When the river breeze blows, some spots feel relatively cool even at midday, so decide in advance where you will rest.

During Holy Week (the week before Easter), prayers of the Way of the Cross and many pilgrims fill the site, and there are many events. The exact schedule differs every year, so check the parish announcements for
March–April
. How events are run can change from year to year.
An old well remains within the church grounds, where you can imagine traces of the Spanish-era town. For safety, do not climb onto the edge of the well.

blocks.title: One to two hours of slow walking

children.text: The sculptures are widely spread, so it works well as a slow walk of about
1–2 hours
. Avoid the hot midday and go in the early morning or late afternoon.

You can buy snacks and drinks around the hill and at the town market. During Holy Week temporary stalls increase. When choosing food, check hygiene with your own eyes, and keep a little cash in small bills ready.

items.subtitle: A round trip from Tuguegarao to Iguig

See the exterior of St. James Church and its buttresses, then look around the interior.
Go up Calvary Hills and walk the stations in order from the first to the fourteenth.
Rest in a shaded spot among the sculptures, drink some water and sort through your photos.
From the stairway behind the church, look out at the Cagayan River and rest for a while.
Have lunch in town and return to Tuguegarao.

During Holy Week roads are congested and crowds are large, so arrive early. The distance between stations is not short, so older or less fit visitors can walk only some of them and still be fine. There are seats and shade among the sculptures, so rest and escape the heat.

items.title: Cagayan church tour
items.subtitle: Combining the cathedral, Iguig and Piat

children.text: Look around Tuguegarao Cathedral and have breakfast.
Go to Iguig and see Calvary Hills and the church.
After lunch, go on to Piat by vehicle.
At Piat Basilica, pay your respects to the image of Our Lady and see the museum.
Return to Tuguegarao and have dinner.
When renting a vehicle for the day, agree on the fare with the driver first.

Take a Tuguegarao coach from a Manila terminal such as Cubao. Allow about
10–12 hours

Renting a vehicle for the day and combining Iguig with Piat and other sites is the most convenient way.
If you take a tricycle from central Tuguegarao, the distance is long enough that you must negotiate the fare. Agree first on a fare that includes waiting for the return.
St. James Church and Calvary Hills are on the same grounds, so you walk between them. It is hot at midday, so bring water and a hat.
The Cagayan Valley is hot and humid at midday. For walking the hill, cool mornings in December–February are best.
Holy Week (usually March–April) is a good time to see the pilgrimage atmosphere but is very crowded and hot. Arrive early and book lodging in advance.
If you want a quiet visit away from Holy Week, weekday mornings are quietest. On weekends and holidays, family visitors increase.

Iguig is a small town without many places to stay. Most visitors stay in central Tuguegarao and come for the day. During Holy Week, hotels in Tuguegarao also fill up early, so book in advance. Lodging and rates change over time, so check recent reviews on booking sites. If you are touring several places in Cagayan along with the churches, using Tuguegarao as your base is convenient for both transport and meals.

For meals, it works well to return to Tuguegarao and eat pancit batil patong (a local dish of noodles topped with an egg) or longganisa. Snacks and drinks are available at shops in town, so buy water before you climb the hill. If you visit at midday, it also helps to buy an iced drink at a town shop and rest. Just check hygiene with your own eyes before you choose.
It is a place of faith, so dress with shoulders and knees covered.
Each station may have an explanation, so read slowly as you walk.
There is little shade at midday, so visit in the early morning or late afternoon. You spend a long time walking among the hills, so bring at least 1 liter of water per person.
See the inside of St. James Church quietly, outside Mass times.
There may be traffic controls during Holy Week, so allow plenty of travel time.
The entrance fee varies by report, so confirm it on site.
Combining Tuguegarao Cathedral and Piat makes the trip efficient.
Take your trash with you and do not climb on or write on the sculptures.
During Holy Week, check the times of the Way of the Cross prayers and step aside when a procession passes.
During Holy Week the crowds and heat are intense and there may be traffic controls. Arrive early and bring plenty of water.
Opening hours and the entrance fee vary by report, so confirm locally.
There are stairs and unpaved paths in many places on the hill, and they are slippery when it rains.
Beware of pickpockets and keep valuables in front of your body.
During events, follow the rules on photography at the sculptures and in the church.
In the rainy season the paths around the church can turn muddy, so wear non-slip shoes.
On days of religious events, avoid loud voices and flash photography so as not to disturb worshippers' prayers.
The central city of Cagayan, close to Iguig, where you can enjoy the cathedral, the museum and local food.
A limestone cave in Peñablanca; go on a separate outing if you want to add nature to your church tour.
A pilgrimage church to the northwest of Iguig that is good to combine on the same day.

If you go down the stairway behind the church, you can see the Cagayan River close up and take a short walk. In the rainy season the water level can rise and be dangerous, so do not go near the water's edge.
